abstract.p: Cryptographic group actions are a leading contender for post-quantum cryptography, and have also been used in the development of quantum cryptographic protocols. In this work, we explore quantum state group actions, which consist of a group acting on a set of quantum states. We show the following results:-If enough copies of each state are provided, statistical (even query bounded) security is impossible.-We construct quantum state group actions and prove them secure in the bounded-copy regime for many computational problems that have been proposed by cryptographers. Depending on the construction, our proofs are either unconditional, rely on LWE, or rely on the quantum random oracle model. While our analysis does not directly apply to classical group actions, we argue it gives at least a sanity check that there are no obvious flaws in the post-quantum assumptions made by cryptographers.-Our quantum state group actions allows for unifying two existing quantum money schemes: those based on group actions, and those based on non-collapsing hashes. We also explain how they can unify classical and quantum key distribution.
